title: Aortic stenosis — exertional syncope + angina + DOE (USMLE CVS case)

properties.cases overview: 65M with recurrent lightheadedness, chest pain, dyspnea on exertion; exertional syncope while climbing stairs. Doppler echo: heavily calcified aortic valve; valve area ~40% normal → severe aortic stenosis pattern. Discussion emphasized afterload/pressure overload physiology, RUSB systolic ejection murmur radiating to carotids, and maneuver differences vs HOCM.
properties.feedback:
Key feedback points from our discussion:
- Corrected mechanism: aortic stenosis causes pressure overload → afterload ↑ → concentric LVH → diastolic dysfunction and exertional symptoms (not primary preload increase).
- Auscultation correction: AS is best heard at RUSB with carotid radiation; LLSB localization more typical for HOCM/VSD/TR patterns.
- Maneuvers: Squatting/leg raise (↑ preload) tends to make AS murmur louder; Valsalva/standing (↓ preload) tends to make HOCM louder.
- Clinical triad anchor: exertional syncope + angina + dyspnea on exertion strongly suggests severe AS.
